slides.title: Angles and Measuring the Earth
slides.html:
Angles and Measuring the Earth

I can name and measure angles and describe how Eratosthenes used them.

geo.title: Angles and Measuring the Earth
geo.target: I can name and measure angles and describe how Eratosthenes used them.

slides.title: Get started
slides.html:
Tape two toothpicks upright on a ball, at different 'cities' on one north-south line. Light them with sunlight, or with a lamp across the room so its rays are nearly parallel. Measure each shadow. Then repeat on a flat board with a flashlight held close. Both setups give different shadow angles. Which one matches what Eratosthenes assumed, and what would tell the two apart?

  • I can name and measure angles and describe how Eratosthenes used them.
  • I can name an angle three ways and measure it with a protractor.
  • I can explain the idea of Eratosthenes' measurement, including what he had to assume.

geo.title: Get started
geo.body:
Tape two toothpicks upright on a ball, at different 'cities' on one north-south line. Light them with sunlight, or with a lamp across the room so its rays are nearly parallel. Measure each shadow. Then repeat on a flat board with a flashlight held close. Both setups give different shadow angles. Which one matches what Eratosthenes assumed, and what would tell the two apart?

  • I can name and measure angles and describe how Eratosthenes used them.
  • I can name an angle three ways and measure it with a protractor.
  • I can explain the idea of Eratosthenes' measurement, including what he had to assume.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html: An angle is two rays with the same endpoint. Its size depends on how far the rays turn apart, not on how long you draw them. Eratosthenes used one angle to estimate the size of the Earth, but only by assuming a model.

geo.title: The big idea
geo.body: An angle is two rays with the same endpoint. Its size depends on how far the rays turn apart, not on how long you draw them. Eratosthenes used one angle to estimate the size of the Earth, but only by assuming a model.

slides.title: Words to know
slides.html:
• angle Two rays that share an endpoint.
  • vertex The shared endpoint of an angle's two rays.
  • ray Part of a line that starts at one point and goes on forever one way.
  • central angle An angle whose vertex is the center of a circle.
  • arc A piece of a circle between two points on it.
  • chord A segment whose endpoints are both on a circle.
  • model assumption A simplifying idea we accept so a real situation fits the math.

slides.title: Common mistake
slides.html:
Pat draws the same angle twice, once with long rays and once with short rays, and says the long one is bigger.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Find and fix the error

An angle's size is how far its rays turn apart. Longer rays don't make a bigger angle.

slides.title: Practice 1
slides.html:
Model: the Earth is a sphere and sunlight is parallel. Two cities on one north-south circle have a center angle of 8 degrees and are 800 km apart along the surface. Estimate the circumference.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

8 degrees is 8/360 of a full turn. So circumference = 800 · 360 / 8 = 36000 km. The shadow-angle step is an assumption here, not a proved fact.

Reveal second check

36000 / 360 = 100 km per degree, and 8 · 100 = 800. It matches.

slides.title: Practice 2
slides.html:
Same model. A center angle of 7.5 degrees matches an 835 km arc. Find the circumference.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

7.5 degrees is 7.5/360 of a turn. Circumference = 835 · 360 / 7.5 = 40,080 km. This is true only inside the model.

Reveal second check

One degree is 835 / 7.5 km. Times 360 gives 40,080 again. Also 40,080 · 7.5 / 360 = 835.

slides.title: Practice 3
slides.html:
Dev uses the straight distance between the cities (the chord) instead of the 835 km curved arc, and does the same fraction trick. Does that still work?

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

No. The angle fraction gives a fraction of the curved arc, not of the straight chord. The chord would need a different method.

Reveal second check

Cut the circle into equal center angles. The arcs fit end to end to make the whole circle. The chords fit together into a polygon, not the circle.

slides.title: Check yourself
slides.html:
Name the angle with vertex O, one ray through A and one ray through B, in three ways.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

Angle AOB or angle BOA, with the vertex letter in the middle. You may also write angle O, but only when O is the vertex of just one angle in the figure.

Reveal second check

Name the given, measurement, assumption, definition or proof you used.
